forecast-period.text: A weak ridge of high pressure develops south of Bight today. This ridge will persist into Thursday before a broad area of low pressure develops over SA on Friday. This low will track eastwards, making way for a new high pressure ridge in the west on Saturday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible isolated showers about windward coasts and the Mount Lofty Ranges. Isolated showers or thunderstorms developing in the far northwest. Maximum temperatures above average in the far northeast, grading to below average elsewhere. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times near the coast.

Showers and thunderstorms about the west and north, possibly reaching the Eyre Peninsula in the late evening. Maximum temperatures generally above average, grading to below average about the southern agricultural area and in the northwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds, tending to fresh northwesterlies in the northwest during the evening.

Scattered showers across the north and west, extending into central and eastern parts in the afternoon, becoming isolated in the northeast. Thunderstorms possible across most districts, becoming more likely in the north and west. Maximum temperature below average in the west, grading to above average elsewhere. East to southeasterly winds across the south and east, with a south to southwesterly change in the west, extending throughout by the evening.

text.p: Isolated showers about coastal districts, possibly extending into the northern agricultural areas and southern pastorals. Isolated thunderstorms possible in the far north. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, below average elsewhere. South to southwesterly winds, freshening during the afternoon.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Generally, less than 2mm in the east, increasing 2 to 5 mm broadly across the agricultural areas with pockets of 5 to 10 mm on the peninsulas. 10 to 20 mm across the far west and with thunderstorms later in the week. Localised falls for 25 to 40 mm in the far northwest with storms.
